claims.canonical_claim: Infertility is only a female health problem.
claims.explanation: Infertility may involve male factors, female factors, combined factors, or remain unexplained.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A man is infertile if pregnancy has not happened after a few months of trying.
claims.explanation: Clinical infertility is generally assessed after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse, with earlier evaluation in some circumstances.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A normal semen analysis proves that a man is fertile.
claims.explanation: Semen analysis is important but cannot by itself confirm individual fertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A low sperm count automatically means a man cannot father a child.
claims.explanation: Sperm count is one factor among several in fertility assessment.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Sperm count is the only semen parameter that matters.
claims.explanation: Count, concentration, motility, morphology and other findings all contribute to interpretation.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Semen appearance alone can tell whether sperm are healthy.
claims.explanation: Appearance cannot establish sperm count, motility or morphology.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: More semen volume always means better fertility.
claims.explanation: Semen volume alone does not determine fertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Semen analysis can diagnose every cause of male infertility.
claims.explanation: Evaluation may also require history, examination and additional investigations.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Male infertility can sometimes be related to hormonal disorders.
claims.explanation: Hormonal disorders can contribute to abnormal sperm production and infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Male infertility can sometimes be related to obstruction of the reproductive tract.
claims.explanation: Reproductive-tract obstruction can interfere with semen transport.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Masturbation automatically causes infertility.
claims.explanation: A blanket causal claim is not supported; ejaculation frequency can change individual semen samples without establishing infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Ejaculating more often permanently depletes sperm.
claims.explanation: Ejaculation changes an individual sample but does not permanently exhaust sperm production.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Longer sexual abstinence always produces better fertility.
claims.explanation: Longer abstinence may increase volume and count but can also be associated with poorer motility or higher DNA fragmentation.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Daily ejaculation necessarily makes a man infertile.
claims.explanation: Frequent ejaculation can alter semen parameters per sample but is not equivalent to infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Ejaculation frequency alone can diagnose fertility.
claims.explanation: Frequency alone cannot diagnose male fertility or infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Masturbation frequency alone proves a sexual disorder.
claims.explanation: Frequency alone is insufficient; distress, loss of control and impairment matter.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Very long abstinence is guaranteed to improve sperm quality.
claims.explanation: Evidence does not support a universal rule that longer abstinence always improves sperm function.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Semen collected by masturbation can be used for clinical semen analysis.
claims.explanation: Masturbation is a standard method for obtaining semen samples for laboratory analysis.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Taking testosterone is a reliable way to improve fertility.
claims.explanation: Exogenous testosterone can suppress sperm production and should not be used as fertility treatment for men seeking fertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Exogenous testosterone can suppress sperm production.
claims.explanation: External testosterone can inhibit reproductive signaling and impair spermatogenesis.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Higher testosterone automatically means higher fertility.
claims.explanation: Fertility depends on sperm production and reproductive function, not simply a higher testosterone value.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Low testosterone always means infertility.
claims.explanation: Low testosterone and infertility are distinct clinical issues with multiple possible causes.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Anabolic steroid use can impair sperm production.
claims.explanation: Anabolic-androgenic steroids can suppress reproductive signaling and impair spermatogenesis.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Stopping prescribed testosterone on your own is the correct way to restore fertility.
claims.explanation: Fertility management after testosterone exposure should be individualized with a clinician.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Every man with low testosterone should automatically receive testosterone therapy.
claims.explanation: Diagnosis and treatment require clinical assessment and fertility goals affect treatment choices.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Hormone levels alone can determine whether a man is fertile.
claims.explanation: Fertility assessment considers reproductive history, semen parameters and other factors.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Smoking has no relationship with male reproductive health.
claims.explanation: Smoking is associated with poorer semen parameters and is a modifiable reproductive-health risk factor.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Quitting smoking is a fertility-supportive lifestyle step.
claims.explanation: Guidelines support discouraging tobacco use as part of reproductive-health prevention.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Heavy alcohol intake can affect male reproductive health.
claims.explanation: High alcohol intake is associated with adverse effects on semen quality and chronic heavy use can reduce testosterone.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Any amount of alcohol makes a man infertile.
claims.explanation: Evidence does not support an all-or-none claim; amount and individual context matter.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Obesity can be associated with poorer male reproductive health.
claims.explanation: Obesity is associated with male infertility and abnormal semen parameters.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Losing weight guarantees that fertility will return to normal.
claims.explanation: Weight loss may improve some reproductive parameters but is not a guaranteed fertility treatment.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Regular physical activity can be associated with better semen parameters.
claims.explanation: Guideline evidence supports associations between recreational physical activity and semen parameters.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: More exercise always means better fertility.
claims.explanation: The relationship depends on intensity, health status and context.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A single lifestyle factor can explain every case of male infertility.
claims.explanation: Male infertility has multiple possible causes including reproductive, hormonal, genetic, medical and environmental factors.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Healthy lifestyle changes can support sexual health and erectile function.
claims.explanation: Physical activity, weight management and cardiovascular-risk reduction may improve erectile function.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Erectile dysfunction is always caused by psychological problems.
claims.explanation: ED can have organic, psychogenic or mixed causes.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Erectile dysfunction can be associated with cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors.
claims.explanation: ED is associated with diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, obesity and metabolic syndrome.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Erectile dysfunction automatically means infertility.
claims.explanation: Erectile function and sperm production are different aspects of reproductive health.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Erectile dysfunction automatically means low testosterone.
claims.explanation: ED has multiple possible causes and is not synonymous with hypogonadism.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: High testicular heat exposure can affect sperm production or semen quality.
claims.explanation: Heat exposure is biologically relevant to spermatogenesis, but magnitude and clinical importance depend on exposure and context.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: One hot bath permanently causes infertility.
claims.explanation: A single heat exposure should not be described as causing permanent infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Hot tubs permanently sterilize men.
claims.explanation: Permanent sterility is an unsupported overstatement; evidence on heat exposure is more nuanced.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A laptop on the lap has been proven to cause male infertility.
claims.explanation: Human evidence does not establish a clear causal infertility effect from ordinary laptop-on-lap exposure.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Tight underwear permanently causes infertility.
claims.explanation: Findings are mixed and current evidence does not support a claim that underwear alone causes permanent infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Underwear choice may influence scrotal temperature.
claims.explanation: Physiologic studies indicate tighter garments can be associated with higher scrotal temperature, while clinical relevance is uncertain.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Any increase in scrotal temperature automatically means infertility.
claims.explanation: Temperature is one factor in spermatogenesis and does not by itself diagnose infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Fever can temporarily affect semen quality.
claims.explanation: Febrile illness has been associated with temporary semen changes, but effects vary and do not equal permanent infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Radiation exposure and ordinary phone use are the same thing.
claims.explanation: Ionizing radiation and radiofrequency exposure are different exposure categories.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Environmental pollutants can contribute to reproductive risk.
claims.explanation: Guidelines identify environmental toxins and pollutants as potential reproductive risk factors.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: One specific food can guarantee higher sperm count.
claims.explanation: No single food is established as a guaranteed fertility treatment.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Fertility supplements are proven to work for every man.
claims.explanation: Guidelines describe the clinical utility of supplements and antioxidants as uncertain or insufficient for routine treatment.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Antioxidant supplements have conclusively been shown to improve male fertility outcomes.
claims.explanation: Evidence is conflicting and major trials have not established consistent benefit.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Taking extra vitamins above nutritional need is guaranteed to improve fertility.
claims.explanation: Correcting deficiency may be appropriate, but excess supplementation is not a universal fertility treatment.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Soy foods automatically lower male fertility because of phytoestrogens.
claims.explanation: A blanket claim that ordinary soy intake causes male infertility is not supported by the evidence base used here.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Drinking more water directly increases sperm count.
claims.explanation: Adequate hydration supports general health, but a direct sperm-count increase from simply drinking more water is not established.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Caffeine automatically causes male infertility.
claims.explanation: Moderate caffeine intake is not established as a universal cause of male infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: More protein automatically means better sperm quality.
claims.explanation: High protein intake is not established as a guaranteed sperm-quality intervention.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A balanced diet is preferable to relying on a single fertility food or supplement.
claims.explanation: Overall health and lifestyle are more appropriate targets than a single guaranteed fertility food.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Over-the-counter fertility supplements are automatically harmless.
claims.explanation: OTC availability does not establish benefit or universal safety.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Marijuana definitely causes male infertility in every user.
claims.explanation: Evidence on marijuana and male fertility is incomplete and conflicting.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Marijuana has no possible reproductive-health relevance.
claims.explanation: Evidence is mixed, but reproductive-health guidance supports discussing and reducing potentially harmful exposure when trying to conceive.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Vaping is proven to be completely safe for reproductive health.
claims.explanation: Current evidence does not support treating electronic nicotine delivery systems as proven safe for reproductive health.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Smoking and secondhand tobacco exposure can have reproductive consequences.
claims.explanation: Evidence supports reproductive-health risks associated with tobacco use and exposure to tobacco smoke.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Anabolic steroid use can negatively affect sperm production.
claims.explanation: Anabolic-androgenic steroids can suppress reproductive signaling and impair spermatogenesis.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Recreational drug use is irrelevant to male reproductive history.
claims.explanation: Infertility histories commonly consider recreational drugs and potentially gonadotoxic exposures.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Alcohol affects every man's fertility in exactly the same way.
claims.explanation: Effects depend on amount, pattern, health status and individual factors.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Heavy chronic alcohol use can reduce testosterone.
claims.explanation: Guideline evidence indicates heavy chronic alcohol use can reduce testosterone.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: You can always tell if someone has an STI by looking at them.
claims.explanation: Many STIs can be asymptomatic, so appearance cannot determine infection status.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Most STIs always cause obvious symptoms.
claims.explanation: Many STIs may have no symptoms.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Using condoms correctly reduces STI risk.
claims.explanation: Correct and consistent condom use reduces the risk of many STIs.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Condoms eliminate all STI risk.
claims.explanation: Condoms reduce risk but do not eliminate infections spread by uncovered skin contact.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Condoms cause infertility.
claims.explanation: Condoms are barrier methods for STI and pregnancy prevention and are not established causes of infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Having no STI symptoms proves that you are STI-free.
claims.explanation: Many STIs are asymptomatic; testing is needed to determine status.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Some untreated genital infections can contribute to reproductive problems.
claims.explanation: Genitourinary infections can contribute to reproductive-tract problems and infertility in some circumstances.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Every STI causes infertility.
claims.explanation: Different infections have different complications; an STI diagnosis does not automatically mean infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Oral sex can transmit some STIs.
claims.explanation: STIs can be transmitted through oral sexual contact.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Only people with many sexual partners can get an STI.
claims.explanation: Any sexually active person can acquire an STI depending on exposure and partner infection status.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: HPV vaccination has relevance for males as well as females.
claims.explanation: CDC prevention guidance includes HPV vaccination as an STI prevention strategy for eligible people.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Alcohol or drugs can increase sexual-risk behavior by lowering inhibitions.
claims.explanation: CDC notes that alcohol or drug use can lower inhibitions and contribute to higher-risk sexual behavior.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A semen analysis is one of the key tests used when evaluating male fertility.
claims.explanation: Semen analysis is a central laboratory assessment in male fertility evaluation.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: One semen sample always gives the complete picture of male fertility.
claims.explanation: Semen parameters can vary and fertility evaluation is broader than one laboratory result.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Semen analysis results should be interpreted in clinical context.
claims.explanation: Laboratory findings are interpreted alongside history, examination and other relevant factors.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Sperm morphology alone determines whether a man can father a child.
claims.explanation: Morphology is one parameter and does not independently determine fertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Sperm motility is relevant to semen assessment.
claims.explanation: Motility is a standard semen characteristic assessed in laboratory evaluation.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A home visual semen check can replace laboratory semen analysis.
claims.explanation: Visual inspection cannot replace standardized laboratory assessment.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Infertility can be unexplained even after evaluation.
claims.explanation: WHO notes that infertility can remain unexplained in some couples.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Male infertility is always permanent.
claims.explanation: Causes vary; some are treatable, modifiable or reversible.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Performance anxiety can never affect sexual function.
claims.explanation: Psychological factors can contribute to sexual dysfunction.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Sexual performance concerns are always evidence of a physical disease.
claims.explanation: Sexual dysfunction can have psychological, organic or mixed contributors.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Stress automatically causes infertility.
claims.explanation: Stress may interact with health and behavior, but stress alone should not be treated as proof of infertility.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Mental health and sexual health can interact.
claims.explanation: Psychological health and sexual function can influence one another.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Pornography frequency alone is enough to diagnose problematic pornography use.
claims.explanation: Frequency alone does not establish a disorder; distress, loss of control and impairment require consideration.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Sexual confidence can be affected by anxiety even without a proven physical disorder.
claims.explanation: Psychological and sexual-function factors can interact, including anxiety-related sexual difficulties.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Sexual dysfunction should always be treated as purely psychological.
claims.explanation: Organic, psychological and mixed causes are all possible.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A single symptom can prove infertility.
claims.explanation: Infertility requires appropriate clinical evaluation; isolated symptoms do not prove it.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A chatbot can diagnose infertility from a questionnaire alone.
claims.explanation: Self-reported information can support education and triage but does not replace clinical evaluation and testing.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: A health app should give a precise percentage probability of fertility from lifestyle questions alone.
claims.explanation: A precise individual fertility probability requires validated predictive evidence and should not be invented from questionnaire data.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Evidence can be insufficient even when a health claim is popular online.
claims.explanation: A safe evidence system should be able to return an insufficient-evidence state instead of forcing a binary answer.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.

claims.canonical_claim: Medical claims should be updated when high-quality evidence or guidelines change.
claims.explanation: A medical knowledge base needs provenance, versioning and periodic review as evidence evolves.
claims.notes: Canonical knowledge unit; not a diagnosis, prevalence estimate, or individual risk prediction.
